summary: State-built 1924 steel tower on Cardigan Mountain in Orange, NH; cab replaced in 2023, equipment reinstalled and part-time staffing back in 2024.

facts.design: 15-foot steel tower fabricated by state crews in 1924; cab replaced in 2023

access.note: Trails to the summit are very well marked. In August 2024 visitors were recorded at the tower while a forestry aid was on duty. During the cab project the state limited summit and trail access on some days and gave no tower access from July 17 through August 31 (the notice gives no year).

visit.trail_note: Reached on foot. The register says the trails and access to the mountain are very well marked.

facts.agency: NH Division of Forests and Lands, Department of Natural and Cultural Resources

events.note: Fabricated by state crews rather than bought from a supplier, per the register. A 1924 state forestry newsletter says four new towers were being erected, one on Cardigan Mountain.

Watchman Wyman Larrabee, 66, reported missing in August 1954 and found dead below his cabin. A medical referee said natural causes and no foul play; forestry officials had said he was struck on the head about a month earlier and did not report it.
Cab replaced. The 2023 chapter report says wet weather delayed the work, which cost $436,000 at Cardigan before contingencies.
Fire-locating equipment reinstalled in June 2024; tower staffed by a forestry aid on August 17, 2024.
Partly staffed by an FFLA member

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 2023 report expected the Cardigan cab work to finish in 2024, but a 2024 Concord Monitor caption says the cab was replaced in 2023. The story gives 2023 for the cab and 2024 for the reinstalled equipment and return to staffing.

The 1954 press reprints differ. One says forestry officials believed the watchman had been struck on the head about a month earlier and had not reported it. The medical referee found natural causes and no foul play. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Record elevation_m 848.3 does not match the 3,121-foot summit in the 1954 press reprints (about 951 m). elevation is not a facts key, so it was not changed; please check it. climbable=true is inferred from the register's stairs and the 2024 visitor reports, not from a published visit rule. No rental information was found. The state's closure notice gives no year, so the access note does not name one. No current 2026 status check was done.
